name: Calling the name of Amitābha (nianfo / nembutsu)

names.name: nenbutsu with the talisman and dance

method_summary: Thinking of Amitābha and calling 'namo Amitābha Buddha' — ten times even at death (Contemplation Sūtra), holding the name one to seven days with undistracted mind (Smaller Sūtra), with faith in the eighteenth vow (Larger Sūtra).
prerequisites: the three minds (Shandao); faith and vow (Ouyi); for Shinshū shinjin, of which the nenbutsu is the expression
duration: whenever walking, standing, sitting or lying, 'until the end of life' (Shandao); counted daily quotas in China and Japan (tens of thousands) or uncounted
signs_of_progress: seeing the Buddha in samādhi (Huaigan: loud recitation brings samādhi)
for Shinshū: joy and gratitude, though its absence is not a sign of failure (Tannishō 9)

warnings.text: Mixed and insincere practice: not one in a thousand is born.
Do not think that because the vow saves evil one may do evil (poison and antidote).
Do not dispute over one calling or many callings.

notes: U43 adds the lineage-specific forms; the three Pure Land sūtras' basis is from U39.

name: The sixteen contemplations of the Contemplation Sūtra

names.name: shiliu guan 十六觀; dingshan (1-13) and sanshan (14-16)

method_summary: Successive visualizations of the setting sun, water and ice, the jewelled ground, trees, ponds, towers, the lotus throne, the images, Amitāyus' body, the two bodhisattvas, one's own birth there, and the nine grades of birth.

warnings.text: Beings' hindrances are heavy, the object subtle and the mind coarse; contemplation is hard to achieve, hence the Buddha urged calling the name.

name: The samādhi of the buddhas standing before one
method_summary: Recollecting Amitābha single-mindedly (the sūtra: for seven days and nights) until one sees him face to face or in a dream, understanding the vision as made by mind. Tiantai made it the 'constantly walking samādhi' of ninety days; summary only.
notes: Huiyuan's Lushan practice; Shandao's walking hymns; Ennin's constantly-walking nenbutsu on Mt Hiei.

name: Dedicating merit (pariṇāmanā)
method_summary: Turning all merit toward awakening for all beings, ideally without apprehending merit, dedicator or goal.

warnings.text: For Shinshū the practitioner has no merit of his own to transfer; the nenbutsu is not said as a memorial for one's parents.

name: Recollection of the Buddha's body and qualities

names.name: Genshin's particular, general and abbreviated contemplations

method_summary: Calling to mind the Tathāgata's golden body, marks and qualities until samādhi, knowing the buddha recollected to be neither form nor formless.

name: The single-practice samādhi (yixing sanmei)
method_summary: Sitting in solitude facing the direction of a buddha and reciting his name continuously until one sees all buddhas in that one and knows the sameness of the dharmadhātu.
notes: Shandao cites it (not contemplating the marks, only calling the name) as scriptural ground for calling.

name: The five gates of mindfulness (Vasubandhu)
method_summary: Worship of Amitābha with the body; praise with the voice by calling his name; single-minded aspiration for birth as śamatha; contemplation of the 29 adornments as vipaśyanā; transfer of merit to all beings.
signs_of_progress: the five gates of merit: approach, the great assembly, the dwelling, the chamber, the garden of play

name: The five right practices (Shandao)
method_summary: Five practices all directed to Amitābha: reciting the Pure Land sūtras, contemplating his land and body, worshipping him, calling his name (the rightly determined act) and praising and making offerings; performed in the four modes.

name: The three meritorious acts (sanfu)
method_summary: Filial care, service of teachers, non-killing and the ten good deeds; taking refuge, keeping the precepts and deportment; arousing bodhicitta, believing in cause and effect, reciting the Mahāyāna sūtras and encouraging others — 'the right cause of the pure acts of the buddhas of the three times'.

name: The seven-day nianfo samādhi retreat (Shandao's practice hall)

names.name: ru daochang nianfo sanmei 入道場念佛三昧

method_summary: In a cleaned room with an image on the west wall, at a chosen period of the month, the practitioner enters for one to seven days in clean clothes, one vegetarian meal a day, recollecting and reciting Amitābha day and night, standing or sitting, confessing at the three or six periods, abstaining from wine, meat and pungent roots. Summary of the text's prescription only.
signs_of_progress: seeing Amitābha's golden body before the mind's eye

warnings.text: Visions that appear are not to be told lightly: good ones are known to oneself, bad ones are to be repented.
The text itself prescribes no sleep for seven days; recorded as the text's instruction only.

name: Deathbed rites for birth (linzhong xingyi / rinjū gyōgi)
method_summary: The dying person faces west (or is moved to a separate hall) before an image of Amitābha, holding a five-coloured cord tied to its hand; attendants burn incense, recite with him, ask what he sees and help him repent evil signs, so that he completes the ten recitations in right mindfulness; those who have taken wine, meat or pungent roots stay away.
signs_of_progress: visions of the lotus-dais and holy assembly (to be recorded)

warnings.text: If relatives who have eaten meat or drunk wine approach, the sick one loses right mindfulness and may die deranged and fall into the evil paths.
Do not wait for the deathbed to begin practising; build the habit now.

notes: Shinshū does not rely on deathbed rites (Mattōshō 1).

name: Assisted recitation for the dying (zhunian)
method_summary: Companions recite Amitābha's name beside the dying, in turns, voice following voice, to support his recollection until the ten recitations are complete; the body is not moved and no one weeps.

warnings.text: Strictly avoid moving the body or weeping, lest the dying one lose right mindfulness.

name: The morning ten recitations (Zunshi's shinian fa)
method_summary: Each morning, facing west with joined palms, one recites the name continuously for the length of a natural breath — one 'recitation' — ten times, voice neither high nor low, then makes the vow of dedication; the breath is used to bind the mind (not a retention practice).

name: Five-tone recitation (wuhui nianfo) of Fazhao
method_summary: The name is chanted by a group in five 'assemblies': slow level tone, slow level-rising tone, neither slow nor fast, gradually faster, and the four syllables 'Amituofo' ever faster; followed by hymns.

warnings.text: Chant with dignity, without laughing or looking about, with a true mind of compassion and not for fame or gain.

name: Pure Land hymns and six-period worship (lizan)
method_summary: Worship and hymns of praise to Amitābha at the six periods of day and night (Shandao's Wangsheng lizan), Tanluan's verses of praise, and in Japan the wasan hymns.

name: Recitation societies (jieshe nianfo)
method_summary: Monks and lay people bind themselves by a common vow to recite and to help one another to birth, meeting regularly — Huiyuan's vow of 402, Song societies, Mao Ziyuan's repentance halls with the five precepts confirmed by five recitations, Ryōnin's nenbutsu register.

name: Loathing practice: contemplating the body's impurity (Jingtu shiyi lun)
method_summary: To turn from the five desires, the aspirant contemplates the body as impure in seven ways (seed, conception, dwelling in the womb, nourishment, birth, the body's contents, death), gradually, even if he cannot yet leave his family; paired with joyful aspiration for the Pure Land.

name: Dancing nenbutsu (odori nenbutsu)
method_summary: Reciting Namu Amida Butsu while dancing in a circle to the beat of drums and bowls, begun by Ippen (1279); performed on stages before crowds; continued in Ji-shū ritual.
notes: Kūya is traditionally credited with a precursor (recalled).

name: Distributing nenbutsu talismans (fusan)
method_summary: Handing to everyone met a slip printed 'Namu Amida Butsu — birth assured — six hundred thousand people', without regard to faith or purity, as instructed by the Kumano oracle.

name: Interfusing nenbutsu with the name register
method_summary: Practitioners inscribe their names in a register and pledge a daily number of recitations, whose merit interfuses with that of all others.

name: Shinshū morning and evening service (gongyō)
method_summary: Recitation of the Shōshinge with the nenbutsu and six wasan before the enshrined image or name of Amida, as arranged by Rennyo; an act of gratitude, not a practice for birth.

name: Enshrining the name as object of reverence (myōgō honzon)
method_summary: Hanging a scroll of the six-, nine- or ten-character name of Amida as the object of reverence in homes and meeting places; Shinran wrote such scrolls and Rennyo distributed the six-character name widely.

name: Hōonkō, the memorial assembly for Shinran
method_summary: The annual assembly of gratitude on the anniversary of Shinran's death, with the reading of Kakunyo's Godenshō and sermons, the central event of the Shinshū year.

name: The fivefold transmission rite (gojū sōden)
method_summary: Jōdo-shū's multi-day rite transmitting the teaching of the school in five stages to monks and lay people, ending in the entrustment of the nenbutsu.
notes: Outline only; details not recalled with confidence.

name: Nenbutsu at special times (betsuji nenbutsu)
method_summary: Intensive nenbutsu for fixed periods (a day to ninety days), and the deathbed practice, as taught in the Ōjōyōshū's sixth chapter.

name: Repentance and vows for birth (Zunshi's rite)
method_summary: Worship of the buddhas, confession of the sins of body, speech and mind, and vows to be born, performed at set times in the Tiantai manner; Mao Ziyuan's dawn repentance of the Lotus school follows this model.

name: Abandoning the body to go to birth (sheshen wangsheng) — restricted
method_summary: Summary only: the rebirth biographies record people who ended their lives (for example by leaping from a tree) out of longing for the Pure Land; Daoxuan's early account attributes such a leap to a man who questioned Shandao, the later Fozu tongji to Shandao himself. Recorded as narrative, not as a practice to be taught.

warnings.text: Shandao's prayer in the account itself asks to die 'without losing right mindfulness'; the tradition's general teaching places birth in the Buddha's vow and recitation, not in the manner of death.

notes: Body-harming: restricted. No method recorded. Explicit warnings by later Pure Land teachers against the act were not verified and are listed as a gap.
